Butrimonys Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Alytus County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Butrimonys had a Jewish population of 282 as early as 1760; the Haskalah spread in the 1880s, and the town supported a yeshiva, two beit-midrash, and a private Russian-language Jewish school, with the Zionist movement strong even in the earlier Hovevei Zion era. The population peaked at 1,919 (80 percent) in 1897, and a Hebrew school operated from 1920 until the 1940 Soviet occupation. By the 1941 German invasion, 750 Jews lived in Butrimonys; they were beaten, raped, robbed, and forced into labor. A ghetto was created on August 29, and on September 9, all of Butrimonys's Jews, along with those from Stakliškės and Birštonas, were shot and buried in two pits — 1,400 people killed within a matter of hours.
